ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r5.claim: The Prophet should patiently receive and convey revelation rather than rush to recite it; God guarantees its collection, preservation, explanation, and elucidation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r5.anchor: The Almighty is revealing it as per His wisdom and expediency.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r6.speaker: قتادة وجماعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r6.claim: They say God will explain and preserve the Qur’an for the Prophet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r6.anchor: قال قتادة وجماعة: أن نبينه لك ونحفظكه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r7.claim: Another view makes the Prophet responsible for explaining it; Qatada also says the explanation distinguishes lawful from forbidden and general from specific.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r7.anchor: وقيل: أن تبينه أنت. وقال قتادة أيضا: أن نبين حلاله وحرامه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains that the Prophet hurried both to memorize and ask about meaning; the command assures preservation and defers questions until recitation ends.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r1.anchor: ثم إن علينا بيانه: إذا أشكل عليك شيء من معانيه، كأنه كان يعجل في الحفظ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r2.speaker: الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r2.claim: Al-Razi reports that early extremist Rafidis alleged the Qur’an was altered, using the supposed lack of connection between these verses and what precedes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r2.anchor: أن القرآن قد غير وبدل وزيد فيه ونقص منه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r3.claim: The author sees a clear contrast: one man rejects resurrection and revelatory signs, while the Prophet eagerly learns, preserves, and presents God’s signs in hope of acceptance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r3.anchor: ويظهر أن المناسبة بين هذه الآية وما قبلها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r8.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r8.claim: The surah describes gathering on Judgment Day in gathering bones and sun with moon, and earthly gathering in collecting and reciting the Quran.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r8.anchor: وذكرت نوعين من الجمع، جمعاً في يوم القيامة وجمعاً في الدنيا

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r10.claim: If the address were to humanity generally, the pronouns could refer to a person’s inward knowledge: do not rush to voice it, since God gathers and recites it and one should follow.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r10.anchor: hesab başında Hakk’ın huzûrunda vicdânındakini acele söyleyip de işin içinden çıkacağım diye telaş etme

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r11.claim: The pronoun’s antecedent is not explicit; a universal-human addressee could make it refer to what is within a person, namely conscience.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r11.anchor: Bu âyetteki بِهِۦ zamirlerinin merci‘i zâhir değildir. Hitab mutlak insana olsaydı

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r12.claim: Because the address is specifically to the Prophet and the passage later names the Qur’an, the pronouns first refer to the Qur’an being revealed; an implied antecedent is sufficient, as at 97:1.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r12.anchor: hitab bilhassa Peygamber’e olmak ve sonra da “Kur’an” denilmiş bulunmak itibariyle bu بِهِۦ zamirinin evvelâ

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r13.claim: The exegetes identify the pronouns as referring to the Qur’an.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r13.anchor: Onun için tefsirler bu بِهِۦ zamirlerinin Kur’ân’a râci‘olduğunu beyan etmektedirler.

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r15.claim: The Prophet should listen while revelation arrives rather than hurry to recite; God undertakes gathering and reciting it, then he follows Gabriel’s completed reading.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r15.anchor: sade dinle, acele okumak için dilini oynatma

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r16.claim: God also undertakes the needed clarification, using five forms of explanation: confirmation, interpretation, alteration, replacement, and necessity; Qur’anic verses explain one another.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r16.anchor: Beyân-ı takrir, Beyân-ı tefsir, Beyân-ı tağyir

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r17.claim: Here “Qur’an” is a verbal noun meaning recitation, though it may also mean the recited text.

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r22.claim: The revelation discussion is integrated with the preceding account of conscience rather than left as a digression, joining the beginning and end of the passage.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r22.anchor: bu âyetleri bu sûrede bir istitrad hâlinde bırakmayarak evvelini âhirine tamamen yapıştırmıştır.

RAZI-FULL:v30p196#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p196#2/r7.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v30p196#2/r7.claim: Al-Qaffāl proposes that the address concerns a person shown his record at resurrection: God reads and gathers his deeds, commands confession, then explains his punishment; this is a strong warning though unsupported by reports.
RAZI-FULL:v30p196#2/r7.anchor: قال القفال : فهذا وجه حسن ليس في العقل ما يدفعه وإن كانت الآثار غير واردة به

RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r1.claim: The verse implies that the Prophet recited alongside Gabriel and asked about difficult meanings during recitation from eagerness to learn; these two practices are addressed by verses 18–19.
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r1.anchor: كان يقرأ مع قراءة جبريل عليه السلام وكان يسأل في أثناء قراءته مشكلاته ، ومعانيه لغاية حرصه على العلم

RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r2.speaker: من جوز تأخير البيان عن وقت الخطاب
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r2.claim: Those who allow clarification to be delayed beyond the initial address cite this verse as evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r2.anchor: احتج من جوز تأخير البيان عن وقت الخطاب بهذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r3.speaker: أبو الحسين
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r3.claim: Abū al-Ḥusayn objects that the apparent wording requires clarification to be delayed, a requirement its proponents do not accept.
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r3.anchor: أن ظاهر الآية يقتضي وجوب تأخير البيان عن وقت الخطاب وأنتم لا تقولون به

RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r4.speaker: أبو الحسين
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r4.claim: Abū al-Ḥusayn says a general indication must accompany the wording to rule out its apparent sense, while detailed explanation may be delayed.
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r4.anchor: أن عندنا الواجب أن يقرن باللفظ إشعارا بأنه ليس المراد من اللفظ ما يقتضيه ظاهره

RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī replies that the wording delays the obligation to explain, not clarification itself, since explanation becomes obligatory only when needed.
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r5.anchor: أن اللفظ لا يقتضي وجوب تأخير البيان بل يقتضي تأخير وجوب البيان ، وعندنا الأمر كذلك لأن وجوب البيان لا يتحقق إلا عند الحاجة

RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r6.claim: He rejects the distinction between general and detailed clarification because “then” covers both; he also rejects al-Qaffāl’s reading as abandoning the plain sense without evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r6.anchor: عن الثاني : أن كلمة ثم دخلت مطلق البيان فيتناول البيان المجمل والمفصل ، وأما سؤال القفال فضعيف أيضا لأنه ترك للظاهر من غير دليل

RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r7.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r7.claim: Al-Qaffāl reads the clause as God subsequently telling Muhammad that explaining it is incumbent upon Him, comparing the phrasing with al-Balad.
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r7.anchor: وهو أن قوله : { ثم إن علينا بيانه } أي ثم إنا نخبرك بأن علينا بيانه ، ونظيره قوله تعالى : { فك رقبة } إلى قوله { ثم كان من الذين ءامنوا }

RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r8.claim: The verse makes explaining an ambiguous text obligatory for God: al-Rāzī’s school grounds this in promise and grace.
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r8.anchor: يدل على أن بيان المجمل واجب على الله تعالى أما عندنا فبالوعد والتفضل

RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r9.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#3/r9.claim: The Muʿtazilites hold that explaining an ambiguous text is required of God by wisdom.

STUDYQURAN:75:16/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r5.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r5.claim: In this report, Ibn ʿAbbās explains “it is for Us to explain it” as God making the Prophet recite it.
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r5.anchor: Then surely it is for Us to explain it [v. 19] means

STUDYQURAN:75:19/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:19/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:75:19/r1.claim: After the Prophet memorizes and recites the Quran, God explains and clarifies it and inspires him to know the intended, legislated meaning.
STUDYQURAN:75:19/r1.anchor: after the Prophet memorizes and recites the Quran, God will explain it to him, clarify it, and inspire him to know its meaning

TAB-FULL:v23p502/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p502/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p502/r7.claim: God undertakes to explain the Qur’an’s lawful and unlawful matters and its rulings in detail.
TAB-FULL:v23p502/r7.anchor: ثم إن علينا بيان ما فيه من حلاله وحرامه وأحكامه لك مفصلة

TAB-FULL:v23p504/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p504/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p504/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the clarification as the Qur’an’s lawful and unlawful matters.
TAB-FULL:v23p504/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {ثم إن علينا بيانه} [القيامة: 19] يقول: حلاله وحرامه

TAB-FULL:v23p504/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p504/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p504/r2.claim: Qatāda says its clarification covers the lawful, avoiding the unlawful, disobedience, and obedience.
TAB-FULL:v23p504/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {ثم إن علينا بيانه} [القيامة: 19] بيان حلاله، واجتناب حرامه

TAB-FULL:v23p504/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p504/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p504/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also explains the clarification as God making the Qur’an clear on Muhammad’s tongue.
TAB-FULL:v23p504/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {ثم إن علينا بيانه} [القيامة: 19] قال: تبيانه بلسانك

TABATABAI:75:16-19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r1.claim: These four verses interrupt the resurrection description with divine etiquette for the Prophet receiving revelation: listen until recitation is complete. Their instruction resembles 20:114.
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r1.anchor: الآيات الأربع في معنى قوله تعالى ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضي إليك وحيه

TABATABAI:75:16-19/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r9.claim: God clarifies the revelation to the Prophet after gathering and reciting it; thumma marks rank-order because explanation follows them.
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r9.anchor: أي علينا إيضاحه عليك بعد ما كان علينا جمعه وقرآنه فثم للتأخير الرتبي

TABATABAI:75:16-19/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r10.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r10.claim: A reported alternative says God explains it to people through the Prophet, who retains it unchanged until reciting it to them.
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r10.anchor: وقيل المعنى ثم إن علينا بيانه للناس بلسانك تحفظه في ذهنك عن التغير والزوال حتى تقرأه على الناس

TABATABAI:75:16-21/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r1.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r1.claim: Some say the Prophet moved his tongue during revelation for fear of forgetting and was told to listen until it ended; the pronoun means what had already been recited to him.
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم في معنى هذه الآيات إن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان يحرك لسانه عند الوحي بما ألقي إليه من القرآن مخافة أن ينساه

TABATABAI:75:16-21/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r3.claim: Another interpreter says these verses concern a person reading his record on Judgment Day, not the Qur’an: God gathers the evidence, demands submission, then explains it if denied.
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r3.anchor: وعن بعضهم في معنى هذه الآيات، الذي اختاره أنه لم يرد القرآن

TABATABAI:75:16-21/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r4.claim: The record-reading view fails because an interrupting passage needs no contextual signs before and after it, and its resemblance to 20:114 supports the Qur’anic reading.
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r4.anchor: ويدفعه أن المعترضة لا تحتاج في تمام معناها إلى دلالة مما قبلها وما بعدها عليه

TABATABAI:75:16-21/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r5.claim: A further view connects the verses to Judgment: do not hasten to ask when it will come; God gathers those destined for it, reveals its description, and clarifies it by the trumpet blast.
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r5.anchor: وعن بعضهم أن الآيات الأربع متصلة بما تقدم من حديث يوم القيامة، وخطاب { لا تحرك } للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:75:16-21/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r6.claim: The Judgment-day reading is untenable to the author.

TABATABAI:75:36-39/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that revelation weighed on the Prophet, who moved his lips to memorize; God promised to gather and recite it, told him to listen, and promised its explanation; thereafter he listened to Gabriel and recited after he left.
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يعالج من التنزيل شدة، وكان يحرك به

TABATABAI:75:36-39/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r11.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes similar reports from Ibn Jubayr and others, but says the fit between this explanation and the verses is obscure.
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r11.anchor: روى ما في معنى صدر الحديث في المجمع عن ابن جبير وفي معناه غير واحد من الروايات، وقد

BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r13.claim: Bayān means explaining unclear Quranic meanings and rulings, revealing the intended sense of general or ambiguous wording.
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r13.anchor: أي بيان ما أشكل عليك من معانيه وأحكامه

BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r14.claim: Thumma allows explanation after the address but not after the time when action is required, since that would impose an impossible obligation.
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r14.anchor: وفي ثم دليل على إنه يجوز تأخر البيان عن وقت الخطاب

TABRISI:75:16/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:16/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:75:16/r7.claim: Bayān is making a meaning distinct to the mind, opposite concealment and obscurity.
TABRISI:75:16/r7.anchor: والبيان إظهار المعنى للنفس بما يتميز به عن غيره ونقيض البيان الإخفاء والإغماض

TABRISI:75:17-24/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:17-24/r9.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:75:17-24/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes the clarification as confirmation of what God has said He will do in the afterlife.
TABRISI:75:17-24/r9.anchor: وقال الحسن: معناه ثم إن علينا بيان ما أنبأناك أنا فاعلون في الآخرة وتحقيقه

TABRISI:75:17-24/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:17-24/r10.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:75:17-24/r10.claim: Qatāda says God will explain its meaning after the Prophet has memorized it.
TABRISI:75:17-24/r10.anchor: وقيل: يريد أنا نبين لك معناه إذا حفظته عن قتادة

TABRISI:75:17-24/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:17-24/r11.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:75:17-24/r11.claim: Another view says God preserves the Qurʾān for the Prophet so he can clarify it to people by reciting it to them.
TABRISI:75:17-24/r11.anchor: وقيل: معناه ثم إن علينا أن نحفظه عليك حتى تبين للناس بتلاوتك إياه عليهم

TABRISI:75:17-24/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:17-24/r12.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:75:17-24/r12.claim: Al-Zajjāj interprets it as God's revelation of an Arabic Qurʾān containing clarification for people.
TABRISI:75:17-24/r12.anchor: وقيل: معناه علينا أن ننزله قرآنا عربيا فيه بيان للناس عن الزجاج

TABRISI:75:17-24/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:17-24/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:75:17-24/r13.claim: The passage shows that the Qurʾān is neither obscure nor enigmatic; it permits delaying clarification after the address, but does not support delaying it past the time when it is needed.
TABRISI:75:17-24/r13.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أنه لا تعمية في القرآن ولا ألغاز ولا دلالة فيه على جواز تأخير البيان عن وقت الحاجة

THALABI:v10p86#2/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p86#2/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p86#2/r14.claim: God's clarification explains the legal limits and what is lawful and forbidden.
THALABI:v10p86#2/r14.anchor: ثم إن علينا بيانه بما فيه من الحدود والحلال والحرام

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:17-28/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:17-28/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:17-28/r3.claim: God undertakes to reveal it as a Qur’an containing clarification for people.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:17-28/r3.anchor: علينا أن ننزله قرآنا فيه بيان للناس

QASHANI:75:17-19/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:75:17-19/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:75:17-19/r3.claim: At the station of detail, God explains the Quran by manifesting its meanings separately in the heart and self.
QASHANI:75:17-19/r3.anchor: عند كونك في مقام التفصيل { إن علينا بيانه } وإظهار معانيه في حيز قلبك

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:16/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:16/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:16/r4.claim: God undertook to explain the revelation.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:16/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:16/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:16/r5.claim: The Prophet was told to remain silent and listen when revelation was recited to him, and he did so.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:16/r5.anchor: vahiy kendisine okunduğunda Hz. Peygamber’in susarak onu dinlemesi emredilmiş, o da böyle yapmıştır (Buhârî, “Tefsîr”, 75; Müslim, “Salât”, 148).

BURHAN:v4p268/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p268/r3.speaker: غير مسمى
BURHAN:v4p268/r3.claim: Some take thumma as equivalent to wāw in these examples, but the author says it retains its original sense.

BURHAN:v2p68/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p68/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p68/r1.claim: In technical usage, muḥkam is what God has made firm through commands and prohibitions and by clarifying lawful and unlawful matters.
BURHAN:v2p68/r1.anchor: وأما في الاصطلاح فهو ما أحكمته بالأمر والنهي وبيان الحلال والحرام

BURHAN:v2p68/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p68/r2.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p68/r2.claim: Reported definitions of muḥkam include unrepealed rulings, the abrogating text, obligations and promise or threat, and material with a single possible interpretation.

BURHAN:v2p68/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p68/r3.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p68/r3.claim: Other definitions call muḥkam text whose meaning is recognized immediately, such as al-Ikhlas and ليس كمثله شيء, or text whose wording recurs.
BURHAN:v2p68/r3.anchor: وقيل الذي تأويله تنزيله بجعل القلوب تعرفه عند سماعه

BURHAN:v2p68/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p68/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p68/r4.claim: Mutashābih originally describes wording that looks alike on its surface while carrying different meanings; the garden fruit is alike in appearance but differs in taste.
BURHAN:v2p68/r4.anchor: وأما المتشابه فأصله أن يشتبه اللفظ في الظاهر مع اختلاف المعاني

BURHAN:v2p68/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p68/r5.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p68/r5.claim: Reported accounts identify mutashābih as resembling verses, abrogated material, stories and parables, opening letters, or matters believers accept while leaving their knowledge to God.
BURHAN:v2p68/r5.anchor: واختلفوا فيه فقيل هو المشتبه الذي يشبه بعضه بعضا وقيل هو المنسوخ الغير معمول به وقيل القصص والأمثال

BURHAN:v2p68/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p68/r6.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p68/r6.claim: Further definitions include matters requiring interpretation, references to the time of the Hour, rain, and death, or wording with several possible meanings and dependence on another passage.
BURHAN:v2p68/r6.anchor: وقيل ما لا يدرى إلا بالتأويل ولا بد من صرفه إليه

BURHAN:v2p68/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p68/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p68/r7.claim: The competing definitions are close: muḥkam can bear one meaning, while mutashābih can bear several or stand only by reference to another passage.
BURHAN:v2p68/r7.anchor: وقيل ما يحتمل وجوها والمحكم ما يحتمل وجها واحدا

BURHAN:v2p68/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p68/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p68/r8.claim: The most reliable explanation expresses the true intended meaning; God assigns clarification to the Prophet and the scholars of his community.
BURHAN:v2p68/r8.anchor: وفصل الخطاب في ذلك أن الله سبحانه قسم الحق بين عباده

BURHAN:v2p68/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p68/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p68/r9.claim: Salaf statements describe what seems ambiguous to limited readers, not the intended divine category of mutashābih; subtle meanings interlock like nearby trees and Qur'anic ordering can make them seem obscure.
BURHAN:v2p68/r9.anchor: وكلام السلف راجع إلى المشتبه بوجه لا إلى المقصود المعبر عنه بالمتشابه في خطابه

BURHAN:v2p68/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p68/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p68/r10.claim: Qur'anic mutashābih in the divine sense means its parts resemble one another in truth, inimitability, good news, warning, and their origin from God; blame falls on those who exploit seeming ambiguity for discord and misguidance.
BURHAN:v2p68/r10.anchor: وأما المتشابه من القرآن العزيز فهو يشابه بعضه بعضا في الحق والصدق والإعجاز والبشارة والنذارة

ITQAN:v3p295/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p295/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p295/r1.claim: When the opening of the sura reached 75:15, the Prophet hastened to retain the revelation; 75:16–19 interrupted that discourse, then it resumed after the instruction and promise of clarification.
ITQAN:v3p295/r1.anchor: صادف أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم في تلك الحالة بادر إلى تحفظ الذي نزل وحرك به لسانه من عجلته خشية من تفلته

ITQAN:v3p295/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p295/r2.speaker: الفخر الرازي
ITQAN:v3p295/r2.claim: Al-Razi compares the apparent interruption to a teacher pausing a lesson to regain a student's attention, then completing the original problem.
ITQAN:v3p295/r2.anchor: قال الفخر الرازي ونحوه مالو ألقى المدرس على الطالب مثلا مسألة فتشاغل الطالب بشيء عرض له

ITQAN:v2p494#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r1.speaker: ثعلب
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r1.claim: Thaʿlab analyzes kallā as a compound of the kāf of comparison and lā, with doubled lām for emphasis and to prevent a two-word reading.
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r1.anchor: مركبة عند ثعلب من كاف التشبيه ولا الثانية شددت لامها لتقوية المعنى ولدفع توهم بقاء معنى الكلمتين

ITQAN:v2p494#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r2.speaker: سيبويه
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r2.claim: Sibawayh and most grammarians treat kallā as a simple particle of rebuke and deterrence, permitting pause before what follows.
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r2.anchor: وقال غيره بسيطة فقال سيبويه والأكثرون حرف معناه الردع والزجر لا معنى لها عندهم إلا ذلك حتى إنهم يجيزون أبدا الوقف عليها

ITQAN:v2p494#3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r3.claim: Some say any surah containing kallā is Meccan because it conveys threat, common in Meccan revelation.
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r3.anchor: حتى قال جماعة منهم متى سمعت كلا في سورة فاحكم بأنها مكية لأن فيها معنى التهديد والوعيد وأكثر ما نزل ذلك بمكة

ITQAN:v2p494#3/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r4.speaker: ابن هشام
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r4.claim: Ibn Hisham objects that rebuke is not apparent in the fashioning verse, the standing of people, or “then its explanation is upon Us”; proposed rebukes are strained, especially after the long separation in the third example.

ITQAN:v2p494#3/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r6.claim: Other scholars say rebuke is not always present in kallā and add a second sense that allows pausing before it and beginning with it.
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r6.anchor: ورأى آخرون أن معنى الردع والزجر ليس مستمرا فيها فزادوا معنى ثانيا يصح عليه أن يوقف دونها ويبتدأ بها

ITQAN:v2p494#3/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r7.speaker: الكسائي
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r7.claim: Al-Kisaʾi says the second sense is “indeed.”
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r7.anchor: ثم اختلفوا في تعيين ذلك المعنى فقال الكسائي تكون بمعنى حقا وقال أبو حاتم بمعنى ألا الاستفتاحية

ITQAN:v2p494#3/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r8.speaker: أبو حاتم
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r8.claim: Abu Hatim reads it as the opening particle alā; Abu Hayyan says none preceded him and al-Zajjaj and others followed.
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r8.anchor: 3253 قال أبو حيان ولم يسبقه إلى ذلك أحد وتابعه جماعة منهم الزجاج

ITQAN:v2p494#3/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r9.speaker: النضر بن شميل
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r9.claim: Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl treats it as a response particle like “yes,” citing “By the moon.”
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r9.anchor: وقال النضر بن شميل حرف جواب بمنزلة أي ونعم وحملوا عليه ﴿ كلا والقمر ﴾

ITQAN:v2p494#3/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r10.speaker: الفراء
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r10.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and Ibn Saʿdān give kallā the future sense “soon”; Abu Hayyan records this.
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r10.anchor: وقال الفراء وابن سعدان بمعنى سوف وحكاه أبو حيان في تذكرته

ITQAN:v2p494#3/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r11.speaker: مكي
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r11.claim: Makkī says kallā is a noun when it means “indeed,” noting a reading with tanwīn and possible derivations from weariness or burden.
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r11.anchor: قال مكي وإذا كان بمعنى حقا فهي اسم وقرئ ﴿ كلا سيكفرون بعبادتهم ﴾ بالتنوين ووجه بأنه مصدر كل إذا أعيا

ITQAN:v2p494#3/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows kallā as a rebuke particle with tanwīn, by analogy with salāsilā.
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r12.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري كونه حرف ردع نون كما في / سلاسلا /

ITQAN:v2p494#3/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r13.speaker: أبو حيان
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r13.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects the analogy: salāsilā restores a noun’s original tanwīn for rhyme, but kallā is not a noun.
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r13.anchor: ورده أبو حيان بأن ذلك إنما صح في / سلاسلا / لأن اسم أصله التنوين فرجع به إلى أصله للتناسب

KHATTABI:v1p39/r6.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p39/r6.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p39/r6.claim: They object that 75:16–19 interrupts the flow from the preceding passage about a person's self-witness to the warning about preferring worldly life, and say each topic should occupy its own section.
KHATTABI:v1p39/r6.anchor: وقد يدخل بين الكلامين ماليس من جنسهما ولا قبيلهما كقوله سبحانه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p223#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p223#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p223#2/r1.claim: Thumma is a coordinating particle denoting sequence with delay; Amr comes after Zayd with an interval.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p223#2/r1.anchor: ثم حرف مبني على الفتح وهو من حروف العطف ويفيد الترتيب والمهلة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p223#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p223#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p223#2/r3.claim: Thumma can function like wāw, “and”; the source applies this to 75:19.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p295#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p295#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p295#2/r1.claim: Kallā is rebuke and restraint: it tells people to stop, denies a preceding claim, or rejects their conduct.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p295#2/r1.anchor: كلا: ردع وزجر، قال الله تعالى: أيطمع كل امرئ منهم أن يدخل جنة نعيم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p295#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p295#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p295#2/r2.claim: After the promise to explain the Qur'an, kallā means stop trying to hasten its recitation.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p295#2/r2.anchor: وقال: ثم إن علينا بيانه (19) كلا بل تحبون العاجلة (20) [القيامة: 19، 20] يريد: انته عن أن تعجل به

NAHHAS:v5p83/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p83/r4.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v5p83/r4.claim: Qatada takes its clarification to be the distinction between what is lawful and unlawful.
NAHHAS:v5p83/r4.anchor: قال قتادة بيان الحلال من الحرام

NAHHAS:v5p83/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p83/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p83/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the clarification as its being made clear by the Prophet’s tongue.

ZAJJAJ:v5p252#2/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p252#2/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p252#2/r7.claim: God undertakes to send it down as clear Arabic without crookedness, containing an explanation for people.
ZAJJAJ:v5p252#2/r7.anchor: أي علينا أن ننزله قرآنا عربيا غير ذي عوج، فيه بيان للناس

ASAD-NOTES:75:16/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:16/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:16/r4.claim: God undertakes to make the revelation's meaning clear.
ASAD-NOTES:75:16/r4.anchor: it will be for Us to make its meaning clear

ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r2.claim: The passage also applies to every believer who reads, listens to, or studies the Qur'an, and should be read with 20:114 and its note 101.
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r2.anchor: both have also a wider import inasmuch as they apply to every believer who reads, listens to or studies the Qur'an

ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r3.claim: While 20:114 warns against hasty conclusions from isolated verses, this passage calls for patient study of the whole message and careful attention to every word and phrase.
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r3.anchor: not to draw hasty - and therefore potentially erroneous - conclusions from isolated verses or statements of the Qur'an

ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r4.claim: Readers and listeners should avoid mechanical fluency or delight in beautiful Qur'anic sound without understanding its message.
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r4.anchor: remain satisfied with the mere beautiful sound of the Qur'anic language without understanding

ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n9/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n9/r1.speaker: Muhammad Abduh
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n9/r1.claim: Muhammad Abduh says that when the Qur'an is read as it ought to be, it becomes its own best commentary.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p214/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p214/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p214/r1.claim: The plural attribution both honors God and reflects that Gabriel actually recites and clarifies under God's command; God directs and the angel transmits.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p214/r1.anchor: ذلك أن القارئ هو جبريل، وليس الله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p214/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p214/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p214/r4.claim: As with the preceding verse, fronting ‘upon Us’ restricts clarification of difficult passages to God.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p214/r4.anchor: فإن تقديم الجار والمجرور يفيد الاختصاص أيضاً ذلك أن تبيين ما أشكل منه مختص به تعالى

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r4.claim: These verses tell the Prophet to be patient amid his opponents’ pressure and repeated demands, while he waits for revelation to answer them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r4.anchor: These verses urge the Prophet (sws) to be patient on the hast iness and various new

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r5.claim: Only revelation gave the Prophet the guidance needed to carry out his grave duty of publicly warning his people; he depended on his Lord at every step.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r5.anchor: He was like a soldier, fighting at a battle front, who could not move even one step without guidance from his Lord.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r7.claim: They also objected that a Qur’an from God should have been revealed all at once, and used such challenges to obstruct the Prophet’s mission.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r7.anchor: Similarly, they would object that if the Qur’ ān was God’s word

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r8.claim: Revelation strengthened the Prophet’s heart and resolve, renewed his soul, and guided his intellect as he faced his opponents.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r8.anchor: It was through divine revelation that his heart would receive strength, his soul would be rejuvenated, his intellect guided

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r9.claim: The Qur’an and Hadith indicate that during divinely wise pauses in revelation the Prophet looked toward heaven; when Gabriel recited, he was eager to learn and preserve every word.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r9.anchor: Consequently, it is evident both from the Qur’ ān and Ḥad īth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r3.claim: The Prophet needed revelation for the strategy of his mission as God’s Messenger.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r3.anchor: All the strategy that needed to be adopted by him in the capac ity of

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r4.claim: Revelation alone could meet his spiritual, moral, and intellectual needs.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r4.anchor: His spiritual, moral and intellectual needs could only be fulfille d

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r5.claim: It supplied guidance for circumstances the Prophet faced and those still to come.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r5.anchor: He would receive from it the guidance needed to face existing and future circumstances.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r6.claim: It enabled him to answer the objections and demands his adversaries continually raised.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r6.anchor: It was through it that he was able to answer the objections and demands which his adversaries would keep posing

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r7.claim: His love of knowledge and care to preserve it also contributed to his eagerness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r7.anchor: His great love for knowledge and his sensitivity in preserving it also contributed very much to it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r8.claim: Though the Prophet’s motives were noble, divine wisdom required gradual revelation, so he was repeatedly urged to be patient.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r8.anchor: it was God’s wisdom that the Qur’ ān be revealed gradually

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r9.claim: The Prophet receives a similar exhortation to patience in Sūrah Ṭāhā.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r9.anchor: In S ūrah Ṭāhā (114-115) too he has been similarly urged.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r10.claim: Here the Prophet is also assured that God will preserve, collect, arrange, recite, and explain the Qur’an, so he can be content with what is revealed and leave its timing to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r10.anchor: here he has been subsequently assured of the preservation of the Qur’ ān also.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r11.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r11.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r11.claim: He should accept the portion revealed, avoid anxiety about its preservation, and trust that each task will be completed at its appointed time.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r11.anchor: He was also not to worry about its preservation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r6.claim: If a passage needs explanation, God will provide it at the proper time; explanatory verses may clarify an earlier directive, abrogate it, or complete it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r6.anchor: verses which were revealed to explain and elucidate a previously revealed directive

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r7.claim: The formula “thus does God explain” commonly follows such explanatory verses and fulfills the promise that God will make the Qur’an clear.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r7.anchor: generally occur after them. They are actually

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r1.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r1.claim: Farāhī accepts the exegetes’ view that haste partly reflected fear of losing Qur’anic material, while adding that the Prophet saw himself entrusted with a grave responsibility.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r1.anchor: I do not differ with this view; however, there are some more details

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r2.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r2.claim: Farāhī says the Prophet feared accountability for losing even a letter, while also seeking more revelation to guide his people; the assurance addresses both concerns.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r2.anchor: he thought that he was being given a great responsibility

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r5.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r5.claim: After collection and arrangement, God explained what He chose, including specifying general directives, supplying supplementary rulings, and narrowing directives.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r5.anchor: furnishing supplementary directives and reducing the scope

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r6.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r6.claim: Farāhī says these conclusions follow from the Qur’an and Hadith: the Prophet recited whole sūrahs in sequence, and Companions memorized and followed that arrangement.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r6.anchor: Consequently, the Prophet (sws) would read out whole sūrahs of the Qur’ ān

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r7.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r7.claim: He says the Prophet directed Companions to place each revealed verse in its assigned position within a particular sūrah, and they obeyed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r7.anchor: direct the Companions (rta) to place the revealed verses

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r1.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r1.claim: An explanatory verse was placed immediately after the material it clarified, or at the end of a sūrah when it explained the whole sūrah’s theme.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r1.anchor: either at the place immediatel y following the verses which needed this explanation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r2.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r2.claim: Explanatory verses generally signal their function with wording that says God explains His verses for people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r2.anchor: They would gener ally be of the wording:

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#4/r1.claim: One explanation is that God will clarify whatever is difficult in the Qur’an’s meanings and rulings.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#4/r1.anchor: بيان ما أشكل عليك من معانيه وأحكامه على ما قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#4/r2.speaker: القاضي أبو الطيب
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#4/r2.claim: Al-Qadi Abu al-Tayyib and his followers infer from ثم that clarification may be delayed beyond the time of the original address.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#4/r2.anchor: واستدل به القاضي أبو الطيب ومن تابعه على جواز تأخير البيان عن وقت الخطاب لمكان ثم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#4/r3.claim: The objection is that بيان may mean making something manifest, without specifically clarifying an ambiguous passage.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#4/r3.anchor: وتعقب بأنه يجوز أن يراد بالبيان الإظهار لا بيان المجمل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#4/r4.claim: Sound reports from the two Sahih collections and others say God will make the Qur’an clear through the Prophet’s tongue, with another wording that He will have him recite it.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#4/r4.anchor: وقد صح من رواية الشيخين وجماعة عن الخبر أنه قال في ذلك ثم إن علينا أننبينه بلسانك في لفظ علينا أن تقرأه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#4/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#4/r5.claim: The report supports taking البيان as the Prophet’s recitation of the whole Qur’an, since only some of it is ambiguous.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#4/r5.anchor: ويؤيد ذلك أن المراد بيان جميع القرآن والمجمل بعضه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r1.claim: God will gather the Quran in the Prophet's breast and enable its recitation; when Gabriel recites it, the Prophet should listen and follow, and God will explain it through his tongue.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r1.anchor: قال علينا أن نجمعه في صدرك، وقرآنه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r3.claim: God will explain whatever meanings of the Qurʾān are unclear.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r3.anchor: بيان ما أشكل عليك من معانيه

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r4.claim: This is evidence that clarification may be delayed beyond the time of the initial address.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r4.anchor: وهو دليل على جواز تأخير البيان عن وقت الخطاب

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r5.claim: The passage reinforces the rebuke against haste: haste is blameworthy even in the most important matter and foundation of religion, and therefore all the more elsewhere; it may also recall an event during revelation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r5.anchor: وهو اعتراض بما يؤكد التوبيخ على حب العجلة

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r6.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r6.claim: Alternatively, the speech addresses the person receiving his record: he stumbles in fear as he hurries to read it, so God promises to gather and read his deeds; he should acknowledge or reflect on the reading, then God explains it through requital.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r6.anchor: وقيل الخطاب مع الإنسان المذكور والمعنى أنه يؤتى كتابه فيتلجلج لسانه من سرعة قراءته خوفا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r3.claim: “Then” signals a delay suited to the greatness of explaining the Qur’an and permits explanation after the initial address, when it is needed; the Prophet may also have hurried to ask about its meaning.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r3.anchor: دالا على جواز تأخير البيان عن وقت الخطاب إلى وقت الحاجة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r4.claim: God guarantees explanation of the Qur’an’s words, arrangement, and meanings, whether Gabriel’s delivery sounds like a bell or ordinary speech; its explanation reaches others through the Prophet and the umma’s scholars.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r4.anchor: أي بيان ألفاظه ومعانيه لك سواء

DURR-FULL:v8p347/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet moved his tongue and lips under revelation’s strain, fearing he would forget; the verses promise collection and recitation, attentive following, and clarification, after which he listened and recited when Gabriel left.
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعالج من التنزيل شدة وكان يحرك به لسانه وشفتيه مخافة أن يتلفت منه

DURR-FULL:v8p347/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet persisted in reciting from fear of forgetting; God undertook to gather and recite it so he would not forget, commanded him to follow it, and to explain its lawful and unlawful rulings.
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يفتر عن القرآن مخافة أن ينساه فقال الله

DURR-FULL:v8p348/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p348/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p348/r4.claim: Qatadah says God’s clarification covers lawful and forbidden matters, obedience, and disobedience.
DURR-FULL:v8p348/r4.anchor: قال: بيان حلاله وحرامه وطاعته ومعصيته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r1.claim: In both places, قرآن is the verbal noun meaning recitation, like غفران and فرقان; Hassan ibn Thabit’s elegy for Uthman witnesses the usage قرآنا.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r1.anchor: و ( قرآن ) في الموضعين مصدر بمعنى القراءة مثل الغفران والفرقان ، قال حسان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r2.claim: In both clauses, علينا expresses God’s undertaking and guarantee.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r2.anchor: ولفظ { علينا } في الموضعين للتكفل والتعهد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r3.claim: ثم marks a higher rank, placing the guarantee of explanation above the guarantee of collecting and reciting the revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r3.anchor: و { ثم } في { ثم إن علينا بيانه } للتراخي في الرتبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r4.claim: God guarantees gathering revelation, its recitation, and—above that—its explanation by the Prophet, preserved in his heart and clear to hearers without consulting a written copy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r4.anchor: أن علينا جمع الوحي وأن تقرأه وفوق ذلك أن تبينه للناس بلسانك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r5.claim: Here البيان means clarifying the Quran’s wording, not its meanings, since the meanings’ clarification accompanies the wording’s arrival.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r5.anchor: فالبيان هنا بيان ألفاظه وليس بيان معانيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r6.speaker: بعض علمائنا
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r6.claim: Some scholars use ثم here to argue that it is permissible to delay clarification after the matter being clarified.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r6.anchor: وقد احتج بهذه الآية بعض علمائنا الذين يرون جواز تأخير البيان عن المبين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r7.claim: That argument is weak: ثم indicates rank, coordinates the whole clause rather than بيان alone, and cannot imply that clarification is always delayed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p350/r7.anchor: لأن التراخي الذي أفادته { ثم } إنما هو تراخ في الرتبة لا في الزمن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422/r1.claim: God makes the Prophet recite the revelation with his tongue: he listened while Gabriel recited, then recited it after Gabriel left, as promised.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422/r1.anchor: نبينه بلسانك فتقرؤه كما أقرأك جبريل وكان إذا أتاه جبريل أطرق فإذا ذهب قرأه كما وعده الله قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422/r2.claim: God undertakes to recompense people on Judgment Day according to the revelation's promises and warnings.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422/r2.anchor: إن علينا أن نجزي به يوم القيامة بما فيه من وعد ووعيد قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422/r3.claim: God undertakes to explain the revelation's rulings, including what is lawful and unlawful.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422/r3.anchor: إن علينا بيان ما فيه من الأحكام والحلال والحرام قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422/r4.claim: God undertakes to send it down as an Arabic Qur'an containing clarification for people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p422/r4.anchor: علينا أن ننزله قرآنا عربيا فيه بيان للناس قاله الزجاج

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r1.claim: God teaches the Prophet to listen rather than race the angel in receiving revelation, promising to collect it in his heart, enable its recitation, and explain it; these are its three stages.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r1.anchor: هذا تعليم من الله عز وجل لرسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في كيفية تلقيه الوحي من الملك، فإنه كان يبادر إلى أخذه، ويسابق الملك في قراءته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r7.claim: After preserving and reciting the Quran, God explains it to the Prophet, clarifies it, and inspires its intended meaning and rulings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r7.anchor: ثم إن علينا بيانه} أي: بعد حفظه وتلاوته نبينه لك ونوضحه، ونلهمك معناه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that revelation caused the Prophet strain and he moved his lips; God told him to listen while Gabriel recited, promised to gather the Quran in his chest, and afterward the Prophet recited it as taught.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعالج من التنزيل شدة، فكان يحرك شفتيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r9.speaker: البخاري ومسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r9.claim: Bukhari and Muslim transmit the report by multiple routes; Bukhari’s wording says the Prophet lowered his head when Gabriel came, then recited after Gabriel left as God had promised.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r9.anchor: وقد رواه البخاري ومسلم، من غير وجه، عن موسى بن أبي عائشة، به (2) ولفظ البخاري: فكان إذا أتاه جبريل أطرق، فإذا ذهب قرأه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p279/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p279/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وعطية العوفي وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p279/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, ʿAtiyya al-ʿAwfi, and Qatada explain the Quran’s clarification as setting out what is lawful and unlawful.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p279/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وعطية العوفي: {ثم إن علينا بيانه} تبيين حلاله وحرامه. وكذا قال قتادة

JISHUMI:v10p7183/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7183/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7183/r16.claim: Bayān is making a meaning apparent to the mind in a way that distinguishes it from other meanings.
JISHUMI:v10p7183/r16.anchor: والبيان: إظهار المعنى للنفس بما يتبين به من غيره

JISHUMI:v10p7186/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7186/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v10p7186/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the promise of clarification as God reminding the Prophet of the Qurʾān.

JISHUMI:v10p7186/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7186/r5.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v10p7186/r5.claim: Qatādah explains the clarification as stating the Qurʾān's rulings and what is lawful and forbidden.
JISHUMI:v10p7186/r5.anchor: نذكر أحكامه وحلاله وحرامه، عن قتادة

JISHUMI:v10p7186/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7186/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7186/r6.claim: Another view says God will explain the Qurʾān's meaning, its rulings, and its clear and ambiguous passages after the Prophet memorizes it.
JISHUMI:v10p7186/r6.anchor: نبين لك معناه إذا حفظته، وبيان أحكامه، ومحكمه، ومتشابهه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p662#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p662#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p662#2/r7.claim: God will explain unclear meanings; the Prophet may have hurried both to memorize and to ask about meaning.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p662#2/r7.anchor: كأنه كان يعجل في الحفظ والسؤال عن المعنى جميعا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r9.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r9.claim: Qatada says God will explain the Quran's rulings, lawful matters, and forbidden matters.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r9.anchor: أحدها : بيان ما فيه من أحكام وحلال وحرام , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says God will explain it through the Prophet's tongue as Gabriel reveals it, so he recites as taught.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r10.anchor: الثاني : علينا بيانه بلسانك إذا نزل به جبريل حتى تقرأه كما أقرأك , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r11.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r11.claim: Al-Hasan says God will repay on Resurrection in accordance with the Quran's promises and threats.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r11.anchor: الثالث : علينا أن نجزي يوم القيامة بما فيه من وعد أو وعيد , قاله الحسن .

MUQATIL:75:19-21/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:75:19-21/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:75:19-21/r1.claim: God will explain the Qur'an's lawful and forbidden matters to Muhammad.
MUQATIL:75:19-21/r1.anchor: يعني أن نبين لك حلاله وحرامه، كما قال الله تعالى:

NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#10/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#10/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#10/r1.claim: God will explain the Qur'an if any of its meanings are unclear to the Prophet.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#10/r1.anchor: إذا اشكل عليك شيء من معانيه

QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r2.claim: The Muslim and Bukhari account says the Prophet listened to Gabriel recite, then recited as taught; Ibn Abbas and Saʿid demonstrate the lip movement.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r2.anchor: عن ابن جبير عن ابن عباس قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يعالج من التنزيل شدة

QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r9.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r9.claim: Qatada says God will explain the Qur’an’s legal limits and lawful and forbidden matters.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r9.anchor: أي تفسير ما فيه من الحدود والحلال والحرام قاله قتادة

QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r10.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r10.claim: Another view takes the explanation as clarifying the Qur’an’s promises and threats and bringing them to pass.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r10.anchor: وقيل: ثم إن علينا بيان ما فيه من الوعد والوعيد

QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r11.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r11.claim: A further view says God will make the Qur’an clear through the Prophet’s tongue.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r11.anchor: وقيل: أي إن علينا أن نبينه بلسانك

ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān links the passage to the contrast between a denier absorbed in sinful desires and someone who preserves, studies, and presents God’s signs in hope of acceptance; opposites reveal each other.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r4.anchor: وقال أبو حيان يظهر أن المناسبة بين هذه الآية وما قبلها أنه سبحانه لما ذكر منكر القيامة والبعث معرضا عن آيات الله تعالى ومعجزاته وأنه قاصر شهواته على الفجور

ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r6.speaker: القفال
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r6.claim: Al-Qaffāl reads the command as addressing the human being when shown his record: fear makes him stumble and rush through it, so he is told not to move his tongue hastily.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r6.anchor: وقال القفال قوله تعالى لا تحرك الخ خطاب للإنسان المذكور في قوله تعالى ينبؤ الإنسان وذلك حال إنبائه بقبائح أفعاله يعرض عليه كتابه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r7.speaker: القفال
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r7.claim: On al-Qaffāl’s view, God promises to assemble the person’s deeds, read them to him, have him acknowledge or consider the record, and then explain its consequences and punishment; this is a severe threat of a detailed account.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r7.anchor: فإنه يجب علينا بحكم الوعد أو بحكم الحكمة أن نجمع أعمالك وأن نقرأها عليك فإذا قرأناه عليك فاتبع قراءته بالأقرار

ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r8.speaker: البلخي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r8.claim: Al-Balkhī and his followers prefer al-Qaffāl’s reading: the pronouns refer to the record implied by 75:13 and the sentence is circumstantial, introduced by an implied saying, at the presentation of the book.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r8.anchor: ومن هنا اختاره البلخي ومن تبعه لكنه مخالف للصحيح المأثور الذي عليه الجمهور

ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r9.speaker: القفال
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r9.claim: Al-Qaffāl's reading that the person receiving his record is addressed differs from the authentic majority transmission that the address is to the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r9.anchor: وقال القفال قوله تعالى لا تحرك الخ خطاب للإنسان المذكور في قوله تعالى ينبؤ الإنسان

ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r1.claim: In the alternative reading, this is a prohibition on asking about the Day’s timing, framed as not opening one’s mouth to rush for its knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r1.anchor: لا تحرك به أي بطلب توقيته لسانك وهو نهي عن السؤال

ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r2.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r2.claim: The Imam suggests the Prophet’s haste may have been explicitly permitted until the prohibition came; al-Ālūsī finds this account problematic.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r2.anchor: وقال الإمام لعل ذلك الاستعجال إن كان مأذونا فيه عليه الصلاة والسلام إلى وقت النهي

ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r4.claim: An alternative reads the direct address as the Prophet, a generic addressee, or any suitable listener; the pronoun refers to the Day of Resurrection, and the sentence interrupts the threat to intensify its terror.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r4.anchor: أنه يكون الخطاب في لا تحرك الخ لسيد المخاطبين حقيقة أو من باب إياك أعني واسمعي أو لكل من يصلح له وضمير به ونظائره ليوم القيامة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r5.claim: On that alternative, the passage means not to hasten to learn the Day’s timing: God will gather creation, reveal its conditions in the Qurʾān, and manifest it at the blast; demanding its date is contrary to wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r5.anchor: إن علينا جمعه ما يكون فيه من الجمع وقرآنه ما يتضمن شرح أحواله وأهواله من القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī says this alternative has serious difficulties and is not the best explanation; he points instead to Zamakhsharī’s account as fitting the Qurʾān’s eloquence and subtle indications.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r6.anchor: وفيه ما فيه وما كنت أذكره لو لا هذا التنبيه واللائق بجزالة التنزيل ولطيف إشاراته ما أشار إليه ذو اليد الطولي جار الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r5.speaker: قتادة وجماعة معه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r5.claim: Qatada and a group understand the clarification as God's undertaking to explain and preserve the Qur'an for the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r5.anchor: قال قتادة وجماعة معه: معناه أن نبينه لك ونحفظكه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r6.speaker: كثير من المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r6.claim: Many exegetes instead say that the Prophet is to explain it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r6.anchor: وقال كثير من المتأولين معناه أن تبينه أنت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r7.speaker: قتادة وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r7.claim: Qatada and others take the clarification to cover lawful and unlawful matters and what is general and what is explained in detail.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة أيضا وغيره معناه أن نبين حلاله وحرامه ومجمله ومفسره
